themes.title: Anthropic eyes history's biggest IPO
themes.summary: Anthropic tells investors it expects to match or top SpaceX's record-setting public offering, the cleanest signal yet that investor appetite for frontier-lab exposure is running hot. The scale of the deal sets a pricing benchmark for the AI complex and feeds directly into OpenAI's own IPO prospectus and every compute owner's capital plans.
themes.angle: The AI boom is now being priced in capital markets, not blog posts.

themes.title: China's AI buildout hits the P&L
themes.summary: Alibaba's profit plunged more than 75% as quarterly capital spending jumped to almost $10 billion to hold its AI position; its CEO expects AI-related annual recurring revenue to reach $10 billion by September. The bluntest evidence yet that hyperscale AI is a margin trade, with direct read-across to Gulf sovereigns standing up data centres.

themes.title: Nvidia China chip: export-control standoff
themes.summary: The Information reported Nvidia will ship a China-specific AI chip by year-end; when news wires amplified it, Nvidia denied the rollout is confirmed. The tension is the live economics of export controls against the margin Nvidia forgoes if it sheds a large share of revenue, and hard to overstate for China's reasoning-model push.

themes.title: Dubai goes fully driverless
themes.summary: Uber began running Baidu's fully driverless Apollo Go robots in Dubai, and the emirate's Robotaxi has now logged more than four million kilometres across over 7,600 rider trips. Dubai is the most permissive large-scale AV market a global platform runs in, a signal for everyone in regional mobility, logistics and impact territory.

themes.title: GCC wires up the AI economy
themes.summary: No single headline, but a coherent regional shift: AI Everything Abu Dhabi frames a push toward $10 trillion in AI-driven enterprises and the world's first AI-native government; a Deloitte/ADGM-backed report argues money-moving AI agents need a new identity layer; Abu Dhabi took Coinbase's tokenised-securities licence; Saudi launched a SAR500,000 cultural-AI incentive and DataVolt wants to export AI compute. Identity, custody and compute are becoming the GCC's competitive envelope.

themes.title: Humanoid robotics: GPT-2 era
themes.summary: Agility Robotics says it is heading to a public listing at a $2.5 billion pre-money valuation as the only pure-play US humanoid maker; The Information likens humanoids to a GPT-2-stage inflection; and the FT asks who is actually buying China's robots, answering with government-backed centres that sell training data back. Capability is real; a broad commercial market is not yet.

themes.title: Inference cost reshapes enterprise AI
themes.summary: Two counter-indicators to the crowded market AI: AT&T is shifting to open-weight models to cut Anthropic inference bills, while Stripe's buy of OpenRouter bets a middleman routing layer still pays in an agentic economy; AWS published enterprise agentic patterns that avoid vendor lock-in. Cost discipline and moats tighten as agents scale.
